answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a bonded notary quorum. Each new agent posts a marble stake and must be attested by a small panel drawn by a raven lottery from existing stakeholders, without replacement. Every notary signs with one quill bound to its own bond, so a single identity can vouch only once; double-signing slashes the entire bond. To forge k fake agents an attacker must lock k separate bonds and still win every random raven draw, so cost grows linearly with identities while success odds shrink.
